title: Introduce generic background purge job framework (idempotent + retryable) with metrics hooks
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Internal: adds a reusable purge job framework for TTL/retention enforcement with idempotent deletes, retry/backoff, and standard metrics/logging; no customer-visible behavior change until wired into individual stores.
description:
Context: We need consistent, safe TTL/retention enforcement across multiple data stores (request/response logs, audit logs, traces/artifacts later). Several store-specific implementations were trending toward duplicate logic (cursoring/pagination, throttling, retries, and metrics). This PR introduces a generic purge job framework that can be reused by store-specific purge implementations.

What this adds: (1) A `purgejob` framework in the background jobs subsystem with a small interface for stores to implement: `PurgeSource` (how to select eligible rows), `PurgeDeleter` (how to delete a batch by IDs/range), and `PurgeCheckpointStore` (persist per-tenant/per-store cursor + last successful watermark). (2) Idempotent + retryable execution semantics: jobs can be re-run safely; deletion operations are expected to be idempotent; checkpoint updates occur only after successful delete batches. (3) Guardrails to prevent DB pressure: bounded batch size, bounded total rows per run, and adaptive sleep/backoff on contention. (4) Standard metrics hooks (Prometheus) and structured logs so SRE can alert on failures/backlog. (5) A CLI-friendly dry-run mode for verifying selection logic without deleting.

Execution model: The framework runs as a scheduled background job. Each run iterates tenants (or a filtered tenant set), evaluates a store-specific "eligibility query" based on a watermark timestamp (e.g., `created_at < now - TTL`) and a monotonic cursor (e.g., id range), deletes in batches, updates checkpoint, and emits metrics. The framework is designed to work even when new eligible rows are concurrently inserted (watermark prevents churn) and when deletions partially fail (retry/backoff + checkpoint remains at last known-good batch).

Metrics (new): `purge_job_runs_total{job,store,result}`; `purge_job_duration_seconds{job,store}` (histogram); `purge_job_batches_total{job,store}`; `purge_job_rows_selected_total{job,store}`; `purge_job_rows_deleted_total{job,store}`; `purge_job_errors_total{job,store,error_class}`; `purge_job_checkpoint_lag_seconds{job,store}` (derived from watermark/last_processed timestamp). Labels intentionally exclude tenant_id to avoid cardinality blow-ups.

Not included: Wiring into request logs/audit logs stores is in follow-up PRs (ENG-18433/ENG-18434). This PR includes a small "example" implementation used only in tests.

Safety notes: Deletion is performed in deterministic batches with a stable ordering key. Checkpoints are updated transactionally with deletion results (best-effort transactional grouping when supported; otherwise two-phase with durable checkpoint only after successful delete). On retry, the same batch can be attempted again without correctness issues. A run-level hard limit (`max_rows_per_run`) prevents runaway deletes and keeps maintenance windows predictable.

Docs/ops: Added README for how to implement a store purge job, how to run locally against staging, and which dashboards/alerts to use once store wiring lands.

Testing: Unit tests for checkpoint behavior, retry semantics, and backoff. Integration-style tests using a sqlite-backed fake store to validate idempotency and cursor progression. CI includes race-enabled tests for the framework package.

purgejob: implement checkpoint store + cursor progression
purgejob: add retry policy with exponential backoff + jitter
observability: add standard purgejob metrics + structured logging fields
tests: add idempotency + partial failure coverage
docs: add purge job framework README + usage examples
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE): Metrics look good, but please do NOT include tenant_id as a label anywhere. Also add an explicit per-run cap on total rows deleted to protect the DB during incidents/maintenance windows.

Benji Okafor (author): Ack. Removed tenant_id from all metric labels; added `max_rows_per_run` (default 250k) and `max_batches_per_run` with flags + docs. Also added log line when run terminates due to cap.
Allison Grant: Can we standardize error classification? We need consistent alert routing (db_timeout vs deadlock vs permission vs unknown).
Benji Okafor (author): Added `error_class` mapping in retry module + exported helper for store implementations. Updated metrics + tests to assert stable classes.
Logan Wright: Backoff policy: please add jitter and ensure we don't hammer primary on partial failures. Also: do we sleep between successful batches?

Benji Okafor (author): Added jittered exponential backoff on retryable errors and an optional `inter_batch_sleep_ms` (default 50ms) that can be tuned per store via job config; also included adaptive increase when db contention signals are observed.

Ethan Park: Checkpoint correctness: ensure we never move the cursor forward if delete returns an error after deleting some rows (common with timeouts). We should treat delete as best-effort but checkpoint must only advance when we can prove completion.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated deleter contract to return `deleted_count` and `err`; runner now advances checkpoint only on `err == nil`. If the deleter can produce partial-delete with error, it must return a retryable error and rely on idempotency to re-attempt; added docs + tests for this scenario.
Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please add a dry-run mode for staging verification and a README that tells oncall what to look at when purge backlog grows.
Benji Okafor (author): Added `--purgejob_dry_run` flag and runbook stub (framework-level). Store-specific runbooks will land with wiring PRs.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Ethan Park. Follow-ups tracked in ENG-18433/ENG-18434 to wire the framework into request logs and audit logs stores.
